archive_15_001.speaker: narrator
archive_15_001.text: The supplier's day-one-hundred update arrived before the cook finished the morning count. The named spring stock was still held in the inspected lower warehouse. Its transport forecast had worsened. A bridge approach on the carriage route had softened beneath repeated thaw, and the district had stopped loaded wagons pending assessment. The supplier could not promise the original early delivery window. Tan read the letter twice, once for the words and once beside the present quantities. The day they had chosen to ask was useful precisely because the answer had become unwelcome.

archive_15_002.speaker: narrator
archive_15_002.text: Dai called the supply meeting that afternoon rather than waiting for the next ordinary board session. Forty charcoal sacks and just over forty resident-days of food had seemed reassuring at supper. They were enough to make a different plan, not enough to ignore a failing one indefinitely. The cook pointed to the wood bundles, which somebody had nearly omitted because charcoal made the more dramatic column. A kitchen could possess grain and warming fuel while lacking the dry cooking fuel its ordinary pot required. Tan added that column to the first page.

archive_15_003.speaker: narrator
archive_15_003.text: The supplier proposed a smaller first consignment by a separate lower pack route, subject to a qualified loaded-route inspection. The existing foot-post path was not automatically suitable for animals. A five-mule train could carry the quoted first food, charcoal and cooking bundles within the carrier's stated net loads if the separate route passed. The remaining stock would follow by carriage when its bridge reopened. Splitting transport increased the agreed delivery charge from twenty-six to fifty-eight copper. The supplier attached the actual carrier quotation, rather than asking the archive to accept a vague winter surcharge.

archive_15_004.speaker: narrator
archive_15_004.text: The first consignment would contain one hundred and twenty food shares, eight five-kilogram charcoal sacks and ten dry cooking bundles. The food components would be weighed and packed from the cook's accepted specification. The carrier would supply its own animal feed and lodging through the quotation, with no hidden call on the archive's resident kitchen. A declared packing allowance sat inside the load limit. The letter promised no supernatural path over snow. It offered a measured transport task which would be cancelled if the inspection found the route unsafe.

archive_15_005.speaker: narrator
archive_15_005.text: Dai asked whether they should release the reserve wage money to pay for an immediate larger delivery. Yue answered before her offer could become an awkward silence: the board could revise an unaccepted employment proposal if it wished, but a larger load still needed a safe route. More money would not make the bridge support it. The chair agreed. The forty-eight spring charcoal sacks and six hundred food shares remained the same order; the problem concerned their movement. They could meet the additional thirty-two-copper transport cost from spring contingency if the smaller route actually passed.

archive_15_006.speaker: narrator
archive_15_006.text: The board authorised that conditional revision. Five hundred and thirty-two copper would cover the unchanged goods and revised delivery, using thirty-two of the spring account's sixty contingency. Twenty-eight remained there, alongside the separate sixty for spring qualified work and the reserved two hundred and eighty for Yue's possible extension. The winter contingency stayed available for present winter failures. Tan sent acceptance of the inspection step, not a statement that the goods had arrived. The supplier would return the route report and actual dispatch plan before putting a pack train on the path.

archive_15_007.speaker: narrator
archive_15_007.text: The cook disliked the first tranche's mixture until she checked its intended role. It would extend the food, warming and cooking margins together rather than deliver a magnificent quantity of one thing while another ran out. She asked for the onions to be packed apart from the dry beans and the oil jars inside their ordinary leak guards. The supplier confirmed those handling terms through the local receiver. He Xi offered to carry the cook's list on his next paid lower loop. His mother asked whether he had already completed that loop for three different people in his imagination.

archive_15_008.speaker: narrator
archive_15_008.text: He laughed and wrote one actual route with its charges. The archive's ordinary correspondence account covered its accepted courier task; private errands remained separate. The cook withdrew a jar-return request which could wait until the next local market. Her choice shortened his load and made the route safer without announcing itself as a grand sacrifice. He took the spring instruction after the current weather check and reached the lower receiver before its closing hour. The receipt returned with the evening bag. A plan had moved one step towards a mule, and no farther.

archive_15_009.speaker: narrator
archive_15_009.text: On day one hundred and one, Tan found damp grit against the coal-store threshold. Snow brought in on boots had melted beside the outer door, and the old sill had wicked it beneath the nearest pallet. The main archive supports remained dry. The surface bypass was within its mark. This was a smaller water route, ordinary enough to have escaped the attention occupied by storms and private-file review. Tan cleared the access space and checked the bottom sacks individually before anyone took the morning fuel. Their outer cloth felt colder than the inner accepted stack.

archive_15_010.speaker: narrator
archive_15_010.text: Six sacks showed enough dampness to exclude them from usable fuel. Tan marked them, moved them to isolated ventilated supports and deducted them from the accepted count. They had been sound stock before the store failure, unlike the three original rejected sacks the merchant had replaced. The distinction mattered for the claim record and for the cook's projection. No supplier owed free replacements for damage caused by the archive's threshold. The sacks were not immediately discarded either. Their recovery would need actual drying and a proper check before any part re-entered the usable count.

archive_15_011.speaker: narrator
archive_15_011.text: Dai looked at the wet sill and asked whether she had failed to approve a repair. Tan found the store inspection from the first autumn week. It had recorded the threshold sound and recommended keeping meltwater away from it. The recent boot traffic and a worn door sweep had changed the exposure. They could improve the control now without rewriting the earlier inspection as a discovery nobody had acted on. The chair asked for the maintenance sequence and current repair estimate. Shame could make a simple failure less legible if everybody tried to give it a more historic cause.

archive_15_012.speaker: narrator
archive_15_012.text: The local joiner quoted fourteen copper for labour, six for materials and two for the accepted delivery, including a sound replacement sweep and a raised dry threshold strip. The board approved twenty-two from winter contingency, reducing it from one hundred and sixty to one hundred and thirty-eight. The joiner could work through the checked village route with his own midday food. The task did not require opening the freight ridge or asking Yue to hold a wet board through a prolonged reinforced stance. He arrived with the right tools and complained chiefly about the old sill's inconvenient angle.

archive_15_013.speaker: narrator
archive_15_013.text: Yue helped clear light empty bins within her ordinary load. She wanted to make the job feel as decisive as the storm's lever, but a threshold strip had no audience and a joiner did not need her channels. He asked her to hold a measuring cord and then corrected where her glove obscured its knot. The correction was so mild that she nearly missed it. She moved her finger, saw the true width and felt relieved. She could contribute to a repair without becoming the repair's extraordinary reason for working.

archive_15_014.speaker: narrator
archive_15_014.text: The six damp sacks went to the small drying bay Tan had cleared under the approved store plan. Air could circulate without sending soot through the paper rooms. No open brazier sat beneath them, and nobody tried to burn wet fuel inside a closed room merely to learn whether it worked. A qualified fuel keeper from the village's existing supply service advised the safe drying check during his paid route. He said some bags might recover sooner than others. The archive's projection assumed none had recovered until his checks supported a number.

archive_15_015.speaker: narrator
archive_15_015.text: Two extra usable charcoal sacks were assigned to the approved drying-room heat over the following days, separately from the normal residence issue. Tan entered that cost before enjoying the possibility of six returned sacks. Drying was work which consumed present fuel and did not guarantee complete recovery. The cook asked whether the calculation still left time for the pack route. Tan showed the updated margin and the inspection date. They could continue ordinary meals and heat while keeping an earlier action point. They were not yet choosing between a resident's supper and a bag's hopeful future.

archive_15_016.speaker: narrator
archive_15_016.text: The drying bay's enclosed stove had a sound flue which the fuel keeper checked before lighting. It warmed the air without an open fire beneath the sacks. Its two extra sacks would be issued across the drying interval and recorded separately. The keeper's professional visit cost two copper from the winter qualified-work fund, leaving one hundred and four there. His fee bought the actual inspection and instructions. It did not buy a promise that damp fuel would be sound merely because the archive had paid somebody to look.

archive_15_017.speaker: narrator
archive_15_017.text: Luo carried the excluded-stock tags to the proper rack after checking their numbers with Tan. His private issue restriction did not prevent this ordinary inventory task. One tag curled near the damp sack, and he replaced its support so the written status remained visible. He told Yue he had once thought a count was a dull form of truth. She asked what he thought now. He said it was still dull, and that might be part of its virtue. The sacks did not become usable because somebody told a moving story about them.

archive_15_018.speaker: narrator
archive_15_018.text: By evening, the joiner had removed the failed sweep and secured the raised strip, leaving the drying area and access path clear. He tested the ordinary door movement and showed the attendant where meltwater should be collected outside. The repair was accepted against its actual estimate. Tan kept the six sacks excluded and the drying cost reserved in the present issue sheet. Beyond the door, the new snow looked harmless for an instant under the yard lamp. Then a worker's boot brought some of it inside, and the attendant used the new brush without needing a speech.

archive_15_019.speaker: narrator
archive_15_019.text: On day one hundred and two, the carrier's route inspector came uphill by the ordinary checked village approach, carrying no spring goods. She met the watcher at the gate and asked for the current surface conditions rather than yesterday's reassuring report. The pack route entered from a lower saddle west of the carriage bridge. It had carried small animal loads in earlier winters, but the carrier would not rely on the old usage without a present inspection. She wanted the district's snow and ground assessment alongside her own judgement of the animals' loads.

archive_15_020.speaker: narrator
archive_15_020.text: Dai showed her the priced specification and the archive's updated quantities. The inspector asked which minimum first delivery would preserve a useful margin in all three columns. Tan showed the accepted tranche rather than inflating it to make a difficult journey seem more worthwhile. The cook asked whether onions counted against the animals' limits like any other goods. The inspector said yes. The cook nodded and removed a wish for another jar of preserved greens which she had not placed on the actual order. It was pleasant to wish; the invoice did not need to carry every wish uphill.

archive_15_021.speaker: narrator
archive_15_021.text: The inspector's five-mule proposal used a forty-kilogram net load limit on each animal, with the actual packing included in the consignment's weighed total. The animals' own condition and the route's combined live-load support were separate checks. She would not use the net goods limit as proof that a bridge could bear an animal. Two handlers and a local guide were included in the revised delivery quotation. Their food and animal feed travelled under their own carriage plan. The archive would receive goods, not an unbudgeted travelling household which needed its winter pot.

archive_15_022.speaker: narrator
archive_15_022.text: Yue asked whether she could accompany the inspection because she knew the local archive turn. The inspector asked what other knowledge she could contribute farther down the route. Yue admitted she did not know it. Her cultivation did not answer the ground assessment, and the ordinary calf had only recently recovered. The inspector had her qualified team and local guide. She thanked Yue for offering and declined the extra traveller. Yue felt briefly useless, then helped the watcher copy the upper-yard condition report which the team actually needed at its receiving end.

archive_15_023.speaker: narrator
archive_15_023.text: The inspector left a dispatch condition sheet before returning to the lower saddle. It named the snow depth, visible edge movement and weather changes which would stop the train. The receiving watcher would need a confirmed message before expecting arrivals, not assume that a promising morning meant the animals had already started. The carrier would assess the packed goods after the route passed. Tan marked those pending steps separately from warehouse reservation. The room acquired another useful unfinished plan, and the cook asked whether somebody could invent a warmer word than pending.

archive_15_024.speaker: narrator
archive_15_024.text: He Xi proposed simmering. The cook said simmering implied there was already something in the pot. Luo proposed waiting. She said waiting was honest but lacked seasoning. Sun, visiting the public desk to arrange her eventual donated print copies, declined to solve the vocabulary question. She had written a fish, not an administrative dictionary. He Xi asked whether an administrative fish would be possible. She said it would require a very small hook and a long account of why nobody had approved the bait. The cook went back to her actual beans.

archive_15_025.speaker: narrator
archive_15_025.text: Sun's proposed donation consisted of one corrected fish card from her author's copy provision, with its current publication terms. She wanted the new work's date and credit recorded as carefully as an old fable's provenance. The pupil's snail remained the pupil's separate decision. Dai could accept the fish into the local-print collection under the stated teaching and reading terms; she could not put Sun's manuscript drafts in the same acquisition by assuming the printed card included them. Sun left the card for the actual accession review and carried her manuscript home.

archive_15_026.speaker: narrator
archive_15_026.text: The assistant asked whether the catalogue should call Sun a retired copyist or an author. Sun said it could name both where relevant, but her present story did not need retirement as its leading fact. Luo suggested contemporary writer. She asked contemporary with whom. The assistant changed the entry to the plain composition and publication dates, followed by the chosen name. Sun approved that description and asked for a copy of the final catalogue slip. It would be the first record in the archive about work she had made while no longer employed by it.

archive_15_027.speaker: narrator
archive_15_027.text: Tan checked the drying sacks at the end of that afternoon and found no usable recovery yet. The flued heat and air circulation had changed their surface feel, but a dry outside could hide retained moisture. The keeper's instructions required the actual soundness check before restoration to the fuel count. She kept all six excluded. The second normal residence sack remained separate from the small extra drying issue. At supper she told the cook that the projection had not improved. The cook said an unchanged number was better than a hopeful one which shrank when put in the stove.

archive_15_028.speaker: narrator
archive_15_028.text: The cold strengthened on day one hundred and three. A window seam in the residential wing began to whistle, and the attendant fitted an ordinary removable draught strip from the existing maintenance stock. Nobody sealed the room's required ventilation to make the brazier last longer. The soot check remained on the roster. Yue slept wearing an extra layer and woke with her jaw sore from clenching it. Her ordinary calf was quiet. The rest of her body reminded her that one recovered muscle did not turn winter into a series of obligations it could bear without sleep.

archive_15_029.speaker: narrator
archive_15_029.text: The cook kept the normal food issue and changed its preparation. Beans soaked under the proper covered kitchen routine took less cooking time; the soaking water was handled according to her ordinary safe method. She did not cut resident shares to create an impressive savings figure before a delayed supply. The soft-food portion for the recovering clerk stayed inside the component count, with its substitution recorded. He had returned to shorter desk tasks and still needed his rest. A face back at a table did not automatically restore the full shift which had made it tired.

archive_15_030.speaker: narrator
archive_15_030.text: Luo offered to cover the clerk's heavier catalogue interval. The assistant checked the combined roster before accepting. His supervised private training and ordinary queue work already occupied the afternoon. He could take one admitted public lookup after the shortened shift, while another rostered clerk handled the rest. Luo disliked the smallness of the offer until he noticed the recovering man did not want to spend his convalescence praising it. They agreed on the specific lookup. The man went to rest, leaving Luo with one old road alias and no new reason to be indispensable.

archive_15_031.speaker: narrator
archive_15_031.text: Yue spent a paid planning interval on her proposed public lesson. She made three invented catalogue slips with different kinds of ambiguity and then tried reading them as someone who did not know the archive. Two examples were too clever. A pupil could fail them without learning anything except that adults enjoyed traps. She tore those drafts for ordinary scrap use and kept the example where asking for a date actually improved the answer. Tan said that lesson would make a poor spectacle. Yue said she hoped it would make a good habit.

archive_15_032.speaker: narrator
archive_15_032.text: The teacher visited to examine the plan and asked how a pupil without cultivated channels could take part. Yue said the public lesson's core was ordinary reading, source questions and handling; no channels were needed. A later qualified cultivation session, if offered at all, would be distinct. The teacher asked for places where pupils could disagree with the example's expected answer. Yue added a question about an ambiguous district boundary which even the source could not resolve alone. She would have to demonstrate asking the proper desk, not performing certainty in front of twenty children.

archive_15_033.speaker: narrator
archive_15_033.text: The carrier's next message arrived on day one hundred and four. The lower saddle's old retaining section needed a district inspection before animals could pass. The team had not approved dispatch. Its stopped report named an actual edge movement rather than a vague fear of winter. Dai asked what the district could safely examine within the next weather interval. The answer described a qualified ground team already assigned to that route, with public maintenance responsibility. The archive would keep the supplier reservation and pay no extra unofficial fee for a hopeful man's assurance that his mule knew the way.

archive_15_034.speaker: narrator
archive_15_034.text: He Xi heard that assurance at the market anyway. A trader offered to carry two sacks uphill on his own animal the next morning, claiming that the carrier's caution was intended to increase charges. He Xi asked which route, what actual animal load and whether the receiving watchers had cleared it. The trader named a shortcut closed by the previous ice warning. He Xi declined the offer without pretending to know every mountain path. He returned with the quoted proposal and its actual defect, not a story about outsmarting every older man at the market.

archive_15_035.speaker: narrator
archive_15_035.text: His father asked whether the trader might still go. He Xi said the watcher had received the named unsafe proposal through the proper public safety contact. What happened next was the watcher's task, not a reason for him to follow a loaded mule in secret. His father looked relieved and disappointed by how little adventure the answer allowed. The boy recognised both expressions because he had worn them himself. They walked back to the workshop along the checked street, where the imperfect fish card sat dry beneath its own wrapper on the owner's shelf.

archive_15_036.speaker: narrator
archive_15_036.text: By evening, the archive had accepted no spring goods and regained no damp charcoal. It had repaired the threshold, paid for the keeper's actual advice and obtained a stopped route inspection which explained what needed to change before dispatch. Dai found that report harder to display proudly than a successful delivery receipt. The chair said it belonged in the file because it had prevented a bad journey. Yue saw the report's blank dispatch line and imagined the living animals absent from the cliff. That absence was a result too, though nobody would clap for it.

archive_15_037.speaker: narrator
archive_15_037.text: The sixth winter watch bell on day one hundred and five brought a report from the lower saddle team. The district inspectors had found the old retaining edge sound enough after clearing its loose surface and checking the ground beneath. They had marked the actual animal line, with room for a handler to step aside at the waiting points. The pack carrier's inspector then walked the route herself under the present conditions. Her approval was conditional on the dispatch morning's weather and load checks. The report opened a possibility; it did not send the mules by itself.

archive_15_038.speaker: narrator
archive_15_038.text: The carrier proposed dispatch on day one hundred and nine, with a checked intermediate lodging and expected arrival on day one hundred and eleven if the local weather held. Feed, handlers' meals and the guide's overnight cost remained included in the accepted quotation. A late departure would trigger a new report rather than a secret attempt to recover time after dark. Tan matched the packing list against the first tranche. The quantities were modest enough to leave room within the stated loads for packaging, and important enough that a delay needed to be named promptly.

archive_15_039.speaker: narrator
archive_15_039.text: Dai asked for the actual warehouse weigh sheet before final dispatch. The goods would be one hundred and twenty complete food shares, eight charcoal sacks and ten cooking bundles, not merely that number of untested bags. The supplier confirmed the inspection sequence, including the oil guards and separate vegetable packing. The revised transport total remained fifty-eight copper. Nothing in the successful ground check authorised a new surcharge. Dai was almost disappointed by the absence of an argument. She had prepared herself to defend their remaining contingency and now needed only to confirm the written terms.

archive_15_040.speaker: narrator
archive_15_040.text: The yard watcher practised the receiving sequence with two empty carried boxes. Arrivals would stop below the narrow turn until the cleared yard path and unloading supports were ready. Animals would not stand beside the paper rooms while staff admired the delivery. The handlers would keep control of the train and use the separate stable place arranged in their own lodging plan. He Xi helped mark the ordinary waiting point on his paid local route, where the guide could see it from below. He did not become an extra overnight handler by being familiar with the archive gate.

archive_15_041.speaker: narrator
archive_15_041.text: Yue caught herself planning a reinforced carrying demonstration for the first consignment. The load checks had already assigned ordinary handlers and archive workers to the unloading. Her recovered practice might be available for a separate measured task, but it was not a reason to shift heavier bags onto her merely because she wanted to feel useful. She took responsibility for checking food components beside the cook. A jar's wrong lid or an incomplete share would matter more to this delivery than the way she stood beneath it. The assignment disappointed her pride and suited her actual knowledge.

archive_15_042.speaker: narrator
archive_15_042.text: A second letter in the morning bag came from the benefit fund. The seamstress's authorised record had completed the service test, and her application had been approved for the fund's sixteen-copper widow allowance under its stated rules. The clerk named the village collection desk and the actual identification needed to receive payment. The letter was a decision, not coins in the archive's purse. The assistant delivered its plain update through the seamstress's chosen contact, then placed the fund record with the application support file. Luo heard the outcome only within the review's relevant scope.

archive_15_043.speaker: narrator
archive_15_043.text: The seamstress came to collect her own decision letter before the public session closed. She asked the assistant whether an archive employee needed to accompany her to the payment desk. The answer was no; her accepted identity record and the fund's decision were sufficient under the clerk's instructions. She smiled with unmistakable relief at having one less person to arrange. Her aunt would receive the eight borrowed copper after actual payment. The repaired rear room had already reopened, so she could use the remaining money for her own next choice rather than a roof still waiting to become safe.

archive_15_044.speaker: narrator
archive_15_044.text: She wanted to thank the assistant and did so plainly. She did not ask to meet Luo, and the assistant did not turn that absence into another wound for him to discuss. The letter's authority had come from the fund's evaluation of an authorised source, not from the archive deciding the benefit itself. The review file retained the earlier breach because the good result did not revise its history. The seamstress carried the decision out through the ordinary gate. For her, the most welcome change was that the next room would finally be one where money could be handed over.

archive_15_045.speaker: narrator
archive_15_045.text: On day one hundred and six, she received the sixteen copper at the named village desk and took its signed receipt home. She repaid her aunt eight and kept the remainder in her own purse. Later she bought one fish card for a copper from the licensed run, leaving seven. The card was a gift for a niece who liked unreasonable animals. The seller put its large corrected author credit upwards on the wrapper. Neither trade mentioned the archive's breach. For a few minutes she was a customer choosing a present with money which belonged to her.

archive_15_046.speaker: narrator
archive_15_046.text: Sun heard of the purchase through the seller's stock report. The seller knew nothing of the woman's application. She was pleased that the fish had reached another household, then asked how many cards remained before the selling deadline. His record accounted for the sixty licensed cards, including her author's copy. She could enjoy circulation without granting a second printing. The seller might ask for one in spring if buyers continued to come. She said he could ask, and wrote no permission for a run which nobody had yet proposed.

archive_15_047.speaker: narrator
archive_15_047.text: Tan inspected the drying bags that afternoon with the keeper's written method and still restored none to usable stock. Some had improved enough for a later test, but the interval was not complete. The two extra heat sacks had now actually been issued across the drying days, separate from the seven normal resident sacks used since day ninety-nine. Twenty-five sound sacks remained. The damaged six stayed on their isolated supports. The cook looked at the number and said she was glad the delivery plan began before the room contained only a very interesting drying experiment.

archive_15_048.speaker: narrator
archive_15_048.text: The seven resident days used seventy food shares, leaving three hundred and thirty-five and a half. Seven ordinary cooking bundles left forty-eight and a half. There had been no visiting kitchen meals or overnight guests during this interval; the route inspector and joiner used the food their own assignments covered. Winter qualified work held one hundred and four copper after the keeper's two-copper visit. Winter contingency held one hundred and thirty-eight after the threshold repair. Spring contingency held twenty-eight after the transport revision, and the committed spring goods still stood below the mountain.

archive_15_049.speaker: narrator
archive_15_049.text: Luo placed the fund's successful response beside the correct issue history when the assistant asked him to complete its ordinary index. He did not make the title say his act had secured the allowance. The initial date had been preserved by an existing rule, and the final evaluation used the later authorised evidence. His earlier urgency had named a real need; his breach had not been the only possible path to its answer. Writing that distinction without bitterness took longer than he expected. He indexed the decision, then left its personal details inside the restricted support file.

archive_15_050.speaker: narrator
archive_15_050.text: At dusk, the keeper sent a note scheduling the first full recovery checks for day one hundred and ten. The carrier confirmed its conditional dispatch window. Two different future actions now appeared beside the actual quantities, each with a responsible person and a reason it might stop. Dai closed the supply file and went downstairs without reopening it to feel safer. The cook had begun a new pot. Outside, the threshold strip held the meltwater away from the nearest pallet, and the small repair remained useful even while everybody waited for a much larger arrival.

archive_15_051.speaker: narrator
archive_15_051.text: The evening of day one hundred and six felt longer than the earlier cold evenings. The numbers were lower, the supply plan more complicated and the six damp sacks more conspicuous now that they had their own supports. Nobody was hungry. The cook had issued the ordinary resident shares, and the normal heat remained inside the plan. Yet Yue noticed every time the door opened. A loss which had not become disaster could still make people live as though the room were asking a question through each draught.

archive_15_052.speaker: narrator
archive_15_052.text: Luo turned his herb away from the glass and accidentally bent a small stem. He held it between two fingers, looking more stricken than the plant warranted. Tan brought a thin ordinary support and said it might recover, though she would not sign a botanical certification. He laughed reluctantly and tied the stem loosely. The joke worked because she had noticed the plant rather than his private review. He set the pot back in the warmer part of the residential sill, where it could lean towards morning without touching the window.

archive_15_053.speaker: narrator
archive_15_053.text: Dai was writing the next supplier enquiry when Yue asked whether she ever regretted accepting the winter renewal. She said yes, usually when a pipe or person became less cooperative than the forecast. Regret about a difficult day did not always mean the appointment had been a wrong choice. Yue asked how one told the difference. Dai put the pen down and said sometimes one needed time away from the desk to hear the answer. That was why leave belonged in an appointment before an emergency made it seem necessary.

archive_15_054.speaker: dai_shuren
archive_15_054.text: I have often waited for work to become quiet enough that leaving would prove I was responsible. Work can always find another reason to need someone. My daughter has offered me a room in a warmer district, and I have answered her with years of excellent explanations. I do want the archive to be safe. I also want to see the room she lives in before it becomes another place described only by letters. Those wants are both mine. The board must learn to work with that fact.

archive_15_055.speaker: narrator
archive_15_055.text: Yue admitted that the spring teaching clause interested her more than she had expected. She also wanted to return home without needing an injury to make departure respectable. Dai said the proposed term had an actual end and an intact return reserve, whatever choice Yue made afterward. A final date could become another vague promise if people allowed it. The contract could give her a place to insist upon one. Yue took the offer from her pocket, examined the new teaching page and noticed that her own question had altered the document before she signed anything.

archive_15_056.speaker: narrator
archive_15_056.text: Tan asked whether staying another fifty-six days would make Yue a custodian. Yue said she did not know. Tan said the word sounded grander than the work she had observed her enjoying. She liked comparing a troublesome line, making an ordinary test repeatable and asking a pupil a question whose answer was not already decided. Those were activities she could carry elsewhere. They did not require a permanent archive title. Yue felt oddly disappointed to have her desired work described so plainly, then understood why Dai's proud application sentence had once been difficult to cross out.

archive_15_057.speaker: narrator
archive_15_057.text: He Xi stopped at the public door before close with the returned local receipt. He had eaten at his family's room and brought no errand requiring another pot. He showed Yue a draft of the route-price lesson he hoped to give at school. It included the boy who promised every neighbour a free delivery and ended up needing somebody else to buy his boots. Yue asked whether the boy was him. He said the boy was an invented public training example, then grinned so broadly that she could tell he had borrowed the clerk's phrase for protection.

archive_15_058.speaker: narrator
archive_15_058.text: The teacher had asked him to include something a customer might reasonably dislike about the charges. He had written that paying did not guarantee good weather or an immediate reply from the receiving person. His mother added that a courier should say what happened to an undelivered parcel before claiming the full task complete. He Xi had revised the page accordingly. Yue liked the lesson and asked which part he would let a pupil challenge. He stared at it, then drew a small space beneath the last line. He could find that question tomorrow.

archive_15_059.speaker: narrator
archive_15_059.text: After he left, the watcher made the late yard round and found the threshold brush in its correct place. Its handle was already wearing where everybody reached for it. A useful ordinary object could acquire a history faster than the catalogue noticed. Yue nearly wrote that sentence in her notebook, then decided it sounded like somebody applying for a grant. She drew the brush instead. The drawing's bristles looked like a furious animal. Tan asked whether Sun had begun a new story. Yue said the brush was entitled to its own ambitions.

archive_15_060.speaker: narrator
archive_15_060.text: The residential lamps were lowered on schedule. The drying bay's flue check and limited heat issue remained the attendant's actual task; it was not left running as a hopeful all-night experiment. Tan signed the evening condition note and handed over to the rostered cover. Luo went to his room with the bent herb properly supported. Dai left her supplier draft on the correct tray. Yue put the spring offer beneath her home letter. Each object belonged to a future action, but none required the whole room to stay awake guarding its meaning.

archive_15_061.speaker: narrator
archive_15_061.text: Before sleeping, Yue listened to the wind lose strength around the new door sweep. The sound was smaller, not gone. She understood why the joiner had complained about the sill's angle: the mountain did not offer straight edges merely because an archive preferred them. Somewhere below, inspected beans and charcoal waited beside a carrier's bags and a conditional route sheet. Here, the cook had enough for tomorrow and the people checking it knew the number. Spring was still a proposal which needed a journey. For the first time, Yue could imagine choosing it without pretending the journey was already complete.
